purpose: Author the refrigeration shop guide from its operation records and schematic drawing primitives.
title: Refrigeration bench guide
subtitle: Coil, donor circuit, argon-purged brazing, mounts and commissioning

extra.qualification_scope: Manual sequence and source review; records no completed circuit build, charge or load test

pages.title: Build the cold loop
pages.subtitle: Wind the evaporator, transfer the donor circuit, and prove the installed refrigeration assembly.

actions.title: Follow the physical sequence
actions.body: Coil work: pages 4-8. Donor prep and circuit work: 2-3 and 9-19. Mounting and commissioning: 20-27.

actions.title: Read the pictures
actions.body: Coral marks the current work. Copper is refrigerant tube. Blue marks a tool, gauge or movement. Pictures are schematic; printed dimensions govern.

actions.title: One valve for life
actions.body: The BPV31 goes onto the process tube once. Venting, the argon purge, vacuum and recharge all pass through its flare port, and it stays as the service point.

result.title: CHECK
result.body: Argon flows from the first cut until vacuum starts; the factory drier stays in service throughout.

pages.title: Read the donor's label
pages.subtitle: One label decides the session: the donor must run R600a, and its factory charge is the number the recharge target builds from.

actions.title: Photograph the real labels
actions.body: Record appliance model, refrigerant, factory charge, compressor voltage, frequency and current ratings. Keep each donor's data with its parts.

actions.title: Verify R600a
actions.body: The type must be R600a. Any HFC donor (R-134a, R-410a) is a full stop: this procedure does not apply. Record the factory charge: 15 g Unit A, 23 g Unit B.

actions.title: Mark the assembly
actions.body: Tag Unit A or Unit B and its compressor. Do not infer charge from the cast-stamps or borrow Unit A's electrical lead colors for Unit B.

result.title: DONE WHEN
result.body: The label reads R600a and the factory charge is recorded: 15 g (A) or 23 g (B).

pages.title: Trace what stays
pages.subtitle: Walk every tube while the donor is still intact. Mark the two cuts before dismantling.

actions.title: Keep the useful assembly
actions.body: Compressor, condenser/fan, original terminal cover, grommets and the bonded capillary/suction pair stay together.

actions.title: Remove the ice-making path
actions.body: The finger-plate evaporator and the hot-gas bypass solenoid, line and tee come out. Remove the valve entirely, or leave it in place and never energize it.

actions.title: Keep the factory drier
actions.body: The drier, its brazed-on capillary, the cap-tube helix and the bonded suction pair stay together as one preserved subassembly, at factory length.

result.title: CHECK
result.body: Both donors' topologies are verified. Nothing upstream of the evaporator-inlet cut is disturbed.

pages.title: Reserve both coil tails
pages.subtitle: Cut the dry coil stock with a tubing cutter, with enough copper for the wrap and each separate routed tail.

drawing.value: INLET / shell exit is the datum
OUTLET / shell exit is the datum

actions.title: Use the specified stock
actions.body: GOORY ACR copper, 1/4 in OD x 0.031 in wall. Keep its bore clean and capped. Do not saw refrigerant tubing.

actions.title: Mark the wrap and tails
actions.body: Current nominal stock is about 4.85 m total: 4.06 m fitted wrap plus 335.5 mm inlet and 429.6 mm outlet allowances.

actions.title: Keep the allowances intact
actions.body: Each allowance includes the in-shell route and protrusion. The longer outlet route still leaves the shorter outside working length.

result.title: CHECK
result.body: The two tails are labeled and the ends are round, square, burr-free and protected from dirt.

pages.title: Wind the copper coil
pages.subtitle: Use the printed mandrel groove to place a single layer of tubing without flattening the bore.

actions.title: Start on the correct tail
actions.body: Reserve the inlet allowance, register the first wrap in the groove, and keep the tail on its assigned side.

actions.title: Follow the helix
actions.body: Wind 9.687 wraps at 12.33 mm pitch over 119.4 mm. The mandrel is 123 mm OD. Keep steady contact without crushing or kinking the tube.

actions.title: Remove without bending a tail
actions.body: Slide the coil axially off the mandrel. Inspect every turn and both exits; a flattened or sharply creased tube is not usable.

result.title: DONE WHEN
result.body: The free coil holds one layer and the inlet/outlet tails leave on opposite assigned lanes.

pages.title: Dress the bare wall
pages.subtitle: Install and prove everything that needs direct steel contact before foil, coil or foam covers it.

actions.title: Bond the wall probe
actions.body: Tape the DS18B20, family 0x28, flat against bare carbonator steel in the band below the wind. Insulate its leads and route them upward.

actions.title: Set the reed bridge
actions.body: Use the rod-register azimuth. Calibrate the finished float and both directional liquid crossings before fixing the final bridge position.

actions.title: Apply the foil skin
actions.body: Apply continuous 3M 425 foil between steel and coil. Preserve the proven sensor positions, lead insulation and the bridge's crossing envelope.

result.title: DONE WHEN
result.body: Probe and reed checks are recorded while every contact point is still reachable.

pages.title: Transfer and bond the coil
pages.subtitle: Slip the wound coil over the foil-dressed 127 mm carbonator, then place the freeze-protect probe.

actions.title: Slide the coil into place
actions.body: The wound coil is undersize to hold against the tank. Ease it on without kinking a tail, dislodging a reed or abrading insulated leads.

actions.title: Add the coil probe
actions.body: Tape the DS18S20, family 0x10, flat against suction-end copper at the high/outlet end. The wall probe stays on steel below the wind.

actions.title: Secure and prove
actions.body: Bond the thermal contact with foil. Prove both probe families and lead continuity before the mold guide's pre-pour check hides the surfaces.

result.title: CHECK
result.body: Two different probe families: 0x28 on steel; 0x10 on copper. Neither probe floats in foam.

pages.title: Route the two exits
pages.subtitle: Lower the dressed carbonator into the open shell with one refrigerant tail in each assigned lane.

drawing.value: Measure on the real routed part

actions.title: Clock by the tails
actions.body: The lower/inlet tail takes the port lane. The upper/outlet tail takes the west lane. Avoid torsion where either tail leaves the wrap.

actions.title: Feed through the round holes
actions.body: While lowering the core, feed each bare tail from inside through its 7.5 mm hole. Support the copper while forming broad curves; do not use the shell edge as a former.

actions.title: Measure and seal
actions.body: Leave 200 mm inlet and 175 mm outlet outside the shell. Reject kinks or flattening; burnish 3M 425 collars around both annuli before the foam pour.

result.title: DONE WHEN
result.body: Both protrusions are recorded and the cured core can be supported with no load on the tube exits.

pages.title: Support before teardown
pages.subtitle: Remove only the donor casing and supports that prevent access, while keeping the sealed circuit undamaged.

drawing.value: Lines carry refrigerant, not the assembly's weight.

actions.title: Unplug and identify the leads
actions.body: Keep mains isolated. Photograph the factory-external compressor and fan connections. Retain the terminal/PTC cover and its original retention.

actions.title: Support each body
actions.body: Keep the compressor upright. Support the condenser, fan and evaporator before undoing their fasteners. Copper tubing must not hold their weight.

actions.title: Preserve the useful details
actions.body: Retain grommets and mounting hardware for inspection. Protect condenser fins, the bonded capillary pair and the process stub. Keep Unit B lead identity open until recorded.

result.title: CHECK
result.body: A missing, cracked, altered or loose terminal cover fails the assembly before power is applied.

pages.title: Vent the factory charge
pages.subtitle: The loop opens for the first time through a valve that never comes off. Decompress fully before any flame.

drawing.value: Gauge atmospheric / no hiss / no smell

actions.title: Find the process tube
actions.body: The short copper stub off the compressor, pinched and brazed shut at the factory. It connects to nothing else.

actions.title: Clamp the BPV31 on for life
actions.body: Clamp the saddle on and pierce. It stays as the single permanent service point: venting, argon, vacuum and recharge all use its flare port.

actions.title: Vent outdoors and confirm
actions.body: Open the valve outdoors or under a vent hood, with no ignition source within 3 m. This vents the household donor; it does not authorize venting a rebuilt unit.

result.title: DONE WHEN
result.body: Gauge reads atmospheric, no further hiss, no smell at the valve. Only then is anything cut or heated.

pages.title: Start the argon purge
pages.subtitle: Argon first, cuts second. One continuous low-pressure flow guards the whole loop-open period.

drawing.value: Argon enters at the BPV31 and leaves by both open cuts.

actions.title: Rig it to the BPV31 flare
actions.body: Uniweld RHP400 on the welder's argon cylinder, then the flared 1/4 in ACR stub, Joywayus flare nut and charging hose onto the BPV31 flare port.

actions.title: Flow a few PSI before cutting
actions.body: Open the BPV31 and start low-pressure argon, flowing, not static. Vented is not empty: R600a lingers in the compressor oil and in low spots.

actions.title: Never break the flow
actions.body: Argon runs from the first cut until vacuum begins on page 16. It is the fuel sweep and the factory drier's dry blanket at the same time.

result.title: CHECK
result.body: A lapse in flow lets the factory drier's desiccant take on moisture and invites capillary icing.

pages.title: Cut at the evaporator
pages.subtitle: Remove the ice-making evaporator with argon flowing, leaving the drier, capillary and bonded heat exchanger at factory length.

drawing.value: Keep this length and bonded pair
Argon flows out of both cuts.

actions.title: Cut the suction line
actions.body: Between the evaporator outlet and the compressor inlet, close to the evaporator, with the RIDGID tubing cutter. Argon leaves here.

actions.title: Cut the cap tube at the evaporator
actions.body: At its evaporator-inlet end, with the Mastercool capillary cutter. Drier, cap tube and helix stay untouched at factory length; argon leaves here too.

actions.title: Strip the ice-making path
actions.body: The finger-plate evaporator and the hot-gas bypass solenoid, line and tee come out. The bonded capillary/suction pair stays intact on the compressor side.

result.title: DONE WHEN
result.body: Both cuts are open with argon flowing out of each; drier, cap tube, helix and bonded pair are at factory length.

pages.title: Wet rag on each stub
pages.subtitle: Both joints sit on copper that runs back into a PET-GF shell with cured foam behind it. Protect it before each braze.

drawing.value: Flame / hot gas away from core

actions.title: Soak and wring a rag
actions.body: Cotton shop rag, heavy with water but not running. Do this immediately before each braze; a rag that has been through one braze is dry.

actions.title: Wrap it hard against the shell
actions.body: On the core side of the joint, covering as much of the stub as it reaches. The rag is the heat sink: wrap toward the shell, not the joint.

actions.title: Keep it wet; aim away
actions.body: Re-wet it between passes. Aim flame and hot gas away from the core, toward the compressor side, never along the stub toward the shell.

result.title: CHECK
result.body: After each braze: gloss, sag, dimpling or a scorched-foam smell at the shell exit means it is compromised.

pages.title: Braze the suction coupling
pages.subtitle: Join the upper coil outlet to the factory suction line with an ACR-grade 1/4 in slip coupling, under the flowing argon.

drawing.value: Clean sockets / full intended engagement / no stress
Copper to copper + BCuP-5 = dry joint, under argon

actions.title: Bright copper first
actions.body: Scotch-Brite both tube ODs and the coupling sockets until bright. Keep grit and swarf out of the bore.

actions.title: Stage the joint
actions.body: The coil-outlet stub leaves the wall on the west lane at the factory suction cut. Slide the slip coupling over both 1/4 in ends; no adapter.

actions.title: Braze dry under argon
actions.body: Wet rag on the stub first (page 13). BCuP-5 self-fluxes on copper, so no flux goes into the sealed loop. Flame away from the core.

result.title: DONE WHEN
result.body: A complete fillet ring at both coupling mouths, argon never interrupted, shell exit unmarked.

pages.title: Pinch-swage the capillary
pages.subtitle: No reducer: the 1/4 in coil-inlet stub collapses onto the cap tube and is brazed under the flowing argon.

drawing.value: 1/4 in coil stub onto the ~0.031 in cap tube, under flowing argon.

actions.title: Slide the cap tube in
actions.body: The cap tube cut on page 12 goes into the coil-inlet stub, which leaves the front wall on the port lane.

actions.title: Swage with the Knipex
actions.body: Knipex 86 01 180 smooth parallel jaws, flats not bites: squeeze, rotate 60 degrees, squeeze again, until the stub has closed evenly onto the cap tube.

actions.title: Braze dry with a fresh rag
actions.body: A fresh wet rag hard against the shell exit; page 14's rag is dry. Braze the swaged mouth with no flux, then check the shell exit.

result.title: CHECK
result.body: The cap tube stays at factory length. If it ever changes substantially, a refrigeration tech recalculates it.

pages.title: Pull vacuum
pages.subtitle: First proof of the brazes, and the handoff: argon stops only because the pump takes over.

drawing.value: 15 min on the pump, then valve off:

actions.title: Argon off, manifold on
actions.body: With every braze done, stop argon at the RHP400 and close the BPV31. Swap the argon hose for the manifold's 1/4 in SAE flare; reopen the BPV31.

actions.title: Pull to 500 microns
actions.body: Orion 4 CFM pump (150 micron ultimate) through the Orion manifold. Reach 500 microns or below and hold at least 15 minutes on the pump.

actions.title: Valve off and watch
actions.body: Isolate the pump. No rise for 15 minutes means tight. A rise is moisture (pump longer) or a leak (find it and fix it).

result.title: DONE WHEN
result.body: 500 microns or below, 15 minutes pumping, then 15 minutes valved off with no rise.

pages.title: Meter the recharge
pages.subtitle: The scale is the meter: what the can loses, the loop gains.

drawing.value: Into the vacuum at the BPV31
Close at the target drop, +/-1 g
Start at factory mass + 5-15 g; iterate 1-2 g.

actions.title: Can on the scale, tared
actions.body: Enviro-Safe R600a can on the Smart Weigh Pro (0.1 g). Plumb can to manifold to the BPV31 flare port; open the BPV31.

actions.title: Charge into the vacuum
actions.body: Open the can valve. R600a flows in on its own vapor pressure and the readout falls. Close at the target drop: the can's lost grams are the charge.

actions.title: Start above factory
actions.body: The wound coil holds more than the finger plate. Start at factory mass (15 g A / 23 g B) plus 5-15 g; iterate 1-2 g against frost pattern and suction superheat.

result.title: CHECK
result.body: Charge within +/-1 g of the working target. The target is settled on first run-up (procedure open item 1).

pages.title: Cap the BPV31 for life
pages.subtitle: The valve that vented the donor stays on as the appliance's only service point.

drawing.value: Record net grams on the unit

actions.title: Button up
actions.body: Close the manifold valve and the BPV31, disconnect the manifold and cap the BPV31 flare port.

actions.title: Leave the valve on
actions.body: The BPV31 stays clamped on the compressor process tube as the single permanent service-access point for vacuum, recharge and later service.

actions.title: Record the charge
actions.body: Write down the net grams delivered and the target they were aimed at. The measured charge belongs on the unit and in its record.

result.title: DONE WHEN
result.body: The BPV31 is closed and capped, clamped on as the service point for life, and the charge is recorded.

pages.title: Run up and sweep for leaks
pages.subtitle: First breath: the right current, a cold suction line and silence from the detector at every joint.

drawing.value: Both tie-ins / BPV31 saddle + cap / every thread

actions.title: Energize briefly
actions.body: Through the inline 5 A fast-blow fuse. Expect ~1 A running; the suction line drops cold within a minute or two.

actions.title: Sweep every joint
actions.body: Toptes PT520A or soap solution at both tie-ins, the BPV31 saddle and flare cap, and every threaded connection. Zero hits, zero bubbles.

actions.title: Wait 3 minutes to restart
actions.body: Firmware holds a 3-minute minimum off. A quick restart stalls the motor against head pressure until the overload trips.

result.title: DONE WHEN
result.body: ~1 A draw, suction cold in 1-2 minutes, no detector hit or bubble at any joint.

pages.title: Place the gas sensor first
pages.subtitle: Install the MQ-6 in the open floor strip before the compressor makes the slot hard to reach.

drawing.value: Install before the compressor blocks access.
Card is on edge; lower until it lands on its shoulder.

actions.title: Orient the card on edge
actions.body: The card runs along the west (-X) flank. Mesh faces west into the wall well; its header faces east into the bay.

actions.title: Lower into the grooves
actions.body: Drop the card straight between the two printed posts until it lands on their shoulder. Route its loom without lifting the card or blocking the low floor zone.

actions.title: Check installed response later
actions.body: A located sensor is not a commissioned interlock. Prove module polarity, clean-air behavior and actual compressor shutdown under the approved test method.

result.title: CHECK
result.body: The gas module is reachable, correctly oriented and retained; its threshold/shutdown evidence remains open.

pages.title: Lower the compressor
pages.subtitle: Mount the connected refrigeration assembly without transferring its weight into the copper lines.

drawing.value: Stop at the washer's post landing.

actions.title: Face the power end forward
actions.body: Keep the original covered terminal/PTC assembly intact. Support the cold core and condenser while lowering the plate straight onto all four floor posts.

actions.title: Use the four intended stacks
actions.body: M5 x 10 SHCS with OD25 fender washers, into RX-M5x9.5 inserts. The posts rise through the rubber grommets; keep the grommets seated.

actions.title: Stop at the post crown
actions.body: The washer is intended to land on the post after nominal 0.4 mm flange squeeze. Check the real bearing path and isolation; there is no accepted torque or load-life result.

result.title: DONE WHEN
result.body: All four stacks land without crushing rubber, hanging on tubework or forcing an insert.

pages.title: Seat the condenser and fan
pages.subtitle: Use the printed rails and aft fingers to carry the condenser block above the slab.

drawing.value: Keep fan and grille air paths clear

actions.title: Enter the aft recess
actions.body: Feed the aft end onto the mounting fingers, then slide fore until the front flanges enter the rail grooves and the face meets their shoulder.

actions.title: Close the two mounts
actions.body: Drive the two M3 x 8 screws down through the donor's aft flange holes into the fingers' inserts. Approach the lower screw from aft with the bay still open.

actions.title: Keep the air path open
actions.body: Confirm the native fan's installed flow direction, clear fins and cross-cabinet inlet/exhaust grilles. Inspect every attached line for stress or rubbing.

result.title: CHECK
result.body: The block is supported by its mounts, the fan turns freely and airflow is confirmed on the real donor.

pages.title: Seat the thermal cutoff
pages.subtitle: The 77 C one-shot fuse reads through contact with the outside flank of the retained donor power cover.

drawing.value: Case is live: both contact faces remain insulating.

actions.title: Keep the live case insulated
actions.body: The cover and printed clamp are the insulating contact surfaces. Keep bare case/leads clear of the compressor can and plate; wiring follows the AC schedule.

actions.title: Place the case and clamp
actions.body: Seat the fuse along its channel against the cover flank. Slide the clamp's leaves into the cover-to-plate gap so the clamp rides with the compressor.

actions.title: Inspect the actual fit
actions.body: The fuse must contact the cover without damage or a loose air gap. Nominal CAD diameter does not prove contact across case/print tolerance; preserve required straight lead length.

result.title: HOLD
result.body: Installed retention, contact and insulation need bench evidence before the cutoff is credited as protection.

pages.title: Prove the first start
pages.subtitle: Finish electrical commissioning and leak checks before a brief compressor smoke test.

actions.title: Read real probes
actions.body: Use thermal and status on the shipping firmware. Require family 0x28 on the tank and 0x10 on the coil; de-energized ambient checks are within +/-2 C.

actions.title: Prove the control path
actions.body: Use a commissioned bench control, with gas interlock and condenser fan working. Honor the 3-minute firmware off guard and any longer donor restart requirement.

actions.title: Observe and stop
actions.body: For the empty-core smoke test, 30-60 s is the procedure's brief window. Record actual nameplate-compatible current and falling coil temperature; stop for hum, overload or a leak.

result.title: CHECK
result.body: This proves switching and probe location only. It does not establish water-load performance or lifetime.

pages.title: Prove the loaded cold loop
pages.subtitle: Commission refrigeration with the documented water load and verify the actual control limits.

drawing.value: Ambient / fill / charge / temperatures / cycles / current

actions.title: Confirm current firmware values
actions.body: Tank: on at 4 C, off at 2 C. Coil: trip at -8 C, recover at -5 C. Minimum off 3 min, on 60 s; stale probe after 30 s parks cooling.

actions.title: Run the specified loaded test
actions.body: Record water fill, ambient, actual charge, starting temperatures, pull-down, outlet-water temperature, coil trend, current and cycle timing.

actions.title: Keep acceptance distinct
actions.body: The acceptance document's 8-hour window and 10-70% duty band are proposed defaults. Missing loaded measurements block production acceptance.

result.title: DONE WHEN
result.body: The logged control behavior and load result meet a committed test specification, with no leak alarm.

pages.title: Repair through the full sequence
pages.subtitle: A leak means the full redo: remove the charge, recut, restore argon, rebraze, pull vacuum and recharge.

drawing.value: A charged or leaking circuit never goes directly to heat.

actions.title: Stop and find the leak
actions.body: Isolate power and ventilate. Find the joint with the detector or soap. A gas alarm, repeated freeze trip or overload is diagnosed, not tuned by guessing.

actions.title: Remove the charge at the BPV31
actions.body: Use the handling route for the completed dispenser and recovery equipment rated for flammable refrigerants. The donor vent does not cover a rebuilt unit.

actions.title: Redo the sequence
actions.body: Recut the joint, restore the argon flow from page 11, rebraze with a wet rag, pull vacuum and recharge by mass. Never repair under charge.

result.title: CHECK
result.body: Any route that applies heat before the charge is out and argon is flowing fails this sequence.

pages.title: Keep the unit's evidence
pages.subtitle: The guide supplies order and pictures; the per-unit record establishes which work and measurements were completed.

drawing.value: Vacuum hold / net charge / leak sweep

actions.title: Keep the measured result
actions.body: Attach donor labels, coil/probe checks, shell-exit checks, the vacuum hold, net charge, the leak sweep and installed control/load results.

actions.title: Use the written sources
actions.body: The footer names the responsible procedure or part reference. The README indexes the local documents.

actions.title: Keep this guide manual
actions.body: Rebuild it deliberately when its operation changes. The PDFs and source receipt are committed artifacts; the appliance build does not redraw them.

result.title: CHECK
result.body: Open items stay where refrigerant-loop.md lists them; the unit record shows what was measured.
